course_name_original: Tecnologías de Redes y Sistemas de Comunicaciones
prerequisites: Ability to read and comprehend documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for effective oral and written communication (expression and comprehension), with special emphasis on technical documentation writing.
Capacity for the integration of technologies, applications, services, and systems specific to Computer Engineering, with a generalist character, and in broader and multidisciplinary contexts.
Capacity to understand and apply the functioning and organization of the Internet, the technologies and protocols of new generation networks, component models, middleware, and services.
Analyze the functioning and organization of the Internet network.
Understand new generation network technologies at different levels of the protocol architecture.
Provide quality of service in new generation networks.
Design corporate communication networks with determined QoS levels.
Manage and administer new generation communication networks.

syllabus_topics: Design, sizing and deployment of networks and distribution systems
Management of networks and communication systems
New generation networks and services. Technologies and protocols
Quality of service in communication networks
Communication networks and systems in industrial environments
Basic configuration of a firewall device
Basic network design technologies (HSRP and Etherchannel)
Basic configuration of a VoIP network
Basic security in a local network environment

assessment_methods.method: Individual activities: Elaboration of laboratory practice reports

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, to pass the subject, each of the three parts (work, reports, exam) must be approved with a minimum grade of 5 out of 10. The final grade is calculated as 0.4 * Group Work + 0.2 * Reports + 0.4 * Exam. In the extraordinary call, approved work and reports from the ordinary call are carried over; failed reports or group work must be corrected and resubmitted. A new in-person theoretical exam must be passed with at least 5 points out of 10. For differentiated evaluation, a final in-person exam for theory and practices will be conducted, with the final grade calculated as 0.7 * Theory + 0.3 * Practices. The professor may require a defense of any part of the evaluation to determine the final grade.
